newsitem.title: USA: USDA - sharp decline in Mar/Aug soybean exports.
newsitem.headline: USDA - sharp decline in Mar/Aug soybean exports.

text.p: Soybean exports for the period of March through August may fall by 56 pct from the period of September through February, the U.S. Agriculture Department's Economic Research Service said on Monday.
In its monthly oil crops outlook, the ERS said the hoof- and-mouth disease in Taiwan's swine industry would restrain growth of U.S. soybean exports.

"The upheaval in Taiwan's swine industry is anticipated to curtail growth in 1996/97 exports to 895 million bushels," the report said. "This forecast implies about a 56 percent reduction in March-August exports from September-February."
The report also said that favorable weather has advanced Brazil's soybean harvest "well ahead of average." Export registrations for Brazil already exceed total 1995/96 shipments, it said.

The monthly oil crops outlook report also said U.S. export shipments of sunflowerseed oil have been "very disappointing." Through January, some 237 million pounds had been exported, down from 328 million for the year-ago period, the report said.
Argentina's soybean harvest is underway and the status of first crop soybeans, especially in the province of Buenos Aires, is "quite good," the ERS report said.
But double-cropped soybeans deteriorated in March due to a continuing drought in the provinces of Santa Fe and Cordoba, the report added.
Argentina is expected to still produce a record harvest mailnly as a result of its large production area because national average yields are projected to be below trends due to dry weather.
